content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis changed to descriptive without formal estimand",
      "quote": "Following the Sponsor’s decision to prematurely terminate the study, the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of PFS will no longer be conducted as per the original study protocol. Considering the expected lack of maturity of the data, the analysis of PFS will only be reported in a descriptive manner.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.1 Statistical Hypotheses",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that PFS will only be analyzed descriptively, but no descriptive analysis method (e.g., Kaplan-Meier estimates, median with confidence interval) is specified. Also, the estimand attributes (population, variable, intercurrent events, summary measure) are not fully defined for the revised analysis.",
      "fix": "Specify the descriptive analysis methods for PFS (e.g., Kaplan-Meier curves, median PFS with 95% CI) and define the estimand attributes for the descriptive analysis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Key secondary endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "This section is a summary of the planned statistical analyses of the most important endpoints, including primary and key secondary endpoints.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "9.3 Statistical Analyses",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical analyses section only describes the primary endpoint (PFS). No analysis methods are provided for key secondary endpoints (ORR, OS) or additional secondary endpoints (DOR, CBR, DCR, safety endpoints).",
      "fix": "Add subsections for each secondary endpoint detailing the analysis methods, including descriptive statistics and any estimation approaches."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of intercurrent events for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Start of subsequent anticancer therapy before disease progression as assessed by investigator or death. To be evaluated for progressive disease and survival.",
      "page": 83,
      "section": "9.3.2 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The table for PFS handling of intercurrent events is provided, but no equivalent handling is specified for secondary endpoints like ORR, DOR, CBR, DCR, or OS. For example, how to handle subsequent therapy for ORR is not defined.",
      "fix": "Define intercurrent event handling strategies for each secondary endpoint, especially for response-based endpoints and OS."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis of safety endpoints specified",
      "quote": "Incidence and severity of adverse events, with severity determined according to the NCI CTCAE v5.0",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Safety endpoints are listed in the objectives table, but the statistical analysis section does not describe how safety data will be summarized or compared between treatment groups.",
      "fix": "Add a safety analysis subsection detailing the descriptive statistics and any comparative analyses for adverse events, ECOG, vital signs, and lab tests."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing sample size inputs for revised descriptive analysis",
      "quote": "Originally, the sample size of this study was determined by the primary endpoint; therefore, the study was event driven.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size section only states the original event-driven design. No information is provided on the actual number of participants enrolled or expected, nor any justification for the descriptive analysis sample size. This is a gap for assessing feasibility of the descriptive analysis.",
      "fix": "Provide the actual or expected sample size and explain how the descriptive analysis will be powered or precision-based."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of PFS in primary endpoint section",
      "quote": "PFS, defined as the time from randomization date to the first documented PD, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoint definition in the objectives table says 'first documented PD' but the statistical analysis section says 'first occurrence of progression' and includes censoring rules. The wording is slightly inconsistent, which could lead to ambiguity.",
      "fix": "Align the wording of the PFS definition across the protocol, e.g., use 'first occurrence of progression or death' consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity control for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "No formal testing will be performed for neither the primary nor for the key secondary efficacy endpoints. Accordingly, a control for the overall type I error (α) applying a gate-keeping hierarchical sequential testing method will no longer be implemented.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that no formal testing will be performed, so multiplicity control is not needed. However, if any descriptive p-values are reported, the protocol does not specify how to interpret them or avoid misleading conclusions.",
      "fix": "Add a statement that descriptive p-values will not be interpreted inferentially and no multiplicity adjustment is applied."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for change from baseline endpoints",
      "quote": "Change from baseline ECOG Performance Status",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoints for change from baseline in ECOG, vital signs, and lab tests are listed, but no statistical analysis method is described for these continuous or ordinal endpoints.",
      "fix": "Specify descriptive statistics (e.g., mean change, shift tables) and any inferential methods for these safety endpoints."
    }
  ]
}
